newsitem.title: USA: Ex-brokers to surrender in Escambia Cty next week.
newsitem.headline: Ex-brokers to surrender in Escambia Cty next week.

text.p: Four ex-brokers are now expected to surrender next week to face racketeering charges stemming from the sale of derivative securities to the former Escambia County, Fla., comptroller, a prosecutor said Wednesday.
The four had been expected to surrender this week but that was delayed by logistical problems, said Escambia County State Attorney Russell Edgar.
"I think it's probably going to be toward the middle of next week," Edgar said.

Florida prosecutors filed fraud and racketeering charges Oct 16 against Kent Tippets Black, Joel Lee Hurst, David Eric Lynch and Larry Eugene Muller, all of whom previously worked in the Houston office of First Montauk Financial Corp unit First Montauk Securities Corp.

The charges allege they schemed to defraud Escambia County by selling former comptorller Joseph Flowers unsuitably risky mortgage-backed securities, by inflating the prices of the securities and by lying about the liquidity and risk involved.
The investments cost county taxpayers about $15 million.
First Montauk officials have said they had no knowledge of the transactions until after the four had left the firm.
